subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and k ∈ ℕ. (R0) If X ∈ D_k(U) has a measure representation (μ,v) (IsMeasureRepresentation), then M_W(X) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U. (R1) Any two restrictions (IsRestriction) of X ∈ D_k(U) to the same set A are equal. (R2) If M_W(X) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U, then there is a measure μ with IsMassMeasure X μ such that X has a restriction to every Borel set A, and every restriction S of X to a set A satisfies M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A) for every open W ⊆ U.

Conjunct (R1) gives the uniqueness Y′ = Y of restrictions.

The proof below is that node's accepted, independently audited natural-language proof (its parent-supplied-natural-proof.json), reproduced verbatim.

Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: (P1) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (representation of currents of locally finite mass by the Riesz Representation Theorem, Ch. 1, 4.14; the characterization 2.8 of μ_T; the restriction 2.9), together with the independence of the restriction from the chosen representation that the contract's IsRestriction (2.9) refers to ("the result does not depend on the representation (uniqueness of the vector measure T⃗ μ_T)").

Fact used. (F1) If tsupport ω ⊆ W then |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ M_W(X): if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ is admissible in the definition of M_W(X).

Part (R0): a measure representation forces locally finite mass.
1. Let (μ,v) be a measure representation of X ∈ D_k(U) (IsMeasureRepresentation: for every ω ∈ D^k(U), x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and X(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ), and let W ⊂⊂ U. Choose φ ∈ C_c^∞(U) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 and φ = 1 on the compact set closure(W) ⊆ U. For each I ∈ I(k,P), φ·dx^I ∈ D^k(U), so x ↦ φ(x) v^I(x) is μ-integrable and c_I := ∫_{closure W} |v^I| dμ < ∞.
2. If ω is admissible for M_W (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), then |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| |v(x)|_* ≤ Σ_I |v^I(x)| 1_{closure W}(x), so X(ω) ≤ Σ_I c_I. Hence M_W(X) ≤ Σ_I c_I < ∞.

Part (R1): restrictions are unique.
3. Let S_1, S_2 be restrictions of X to A, via representations (μ_1,v_1), (μ_2,v_2) of X (so A is measurable and S_l(ω) = ∫_A v_l(ω) dμ_l). As in step 1, ∫_K |v_l^I| dμ_l < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U and every I. Hence ν_l^I(B) := ∫_B v_l^I dμ_l (Borel B ⊆ U) defines signed Borel measures on U of locally finite total variation.
4. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(U): ∫ φ dν_1^I = X(φ dx^I) = ∫ φ dν_2^I. Every φ ∈ C_c(U) is the uniform limit of mollifications φ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U) supported in a fixed compact subset K of U; by dominated convergence (|v_l^I| is μ_l-integrable on K) the identity extends to all φ ∈ C_c(U).
5. Hence ν_1^I = ν_2^I on Borel subsets of U: the positive locally finite Borel measures λ_1 := (ν_1^I)⁺ + (ν_2^I)⁻ and λ_2 := (ν_2^I)⁺ + (ν_1^I)⁻ on U (Jordan decompositions) have equal integrals against every φ ∈ C_c(U); locally finite Borel measures on the open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (a locally compact, σ-compact metric space) are regular and are determined by these integrals (Riesz uniqueness, Simon Ch. 1, 4.12; Mathlib `Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported`). So λ_1 = λ_2.
6. Let ω ∈ D^k(U); write ω = Σ_I ω_I dx^I with ω_I := ω(·)(e_I) ∈ C_c^∞(U), so v_l(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) v_l^I(x), and ω vanishes off the compact K := tsupport ω ⊆ U. Then S_l(ω) = Σ_I ∫_{A∩K} ω_I dν_l^I, which by step 5 is the same for l = 1, 2. Thus S_1(ω) = S_2(ω) for all ω, and S_1 = S_2 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

Part (R2): mass measure, existence of restrictions, mass identity. Assume M_W(X) < ∞ for all W ⊂⊂ U. Let N := #I(k,P) and identify a k-covector α with its coefficient vector (α(e_I))_I ∈ ℝ^N; this is an isometry between |·| and the Euclidean norm of ℝ^N.
7. (Extension to continuous forms.) Let K_c(U;ℝ^N) be the continuous maps φ : U → ℝ^N with compact support in U. For such φ choose W ⊂⊂ U with spt φ ⊆ W; componentwise mollification gives test forms ω_ε with tsupport ω_ε ⊆ W for small ε, ‖ω_ε − φ‖ → 0 and |ω_ε| ≤ sup|φ| pointwise (mollification is an average and the Euclidean ball is convex). By (F1), |X(ω_ε) − X(ω_δ)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω_ε − ω_δ‖ → 0, so L(φ) := lim_ε X(ω_ε) exists, does not depend on the approximating sequence, is linear, equals X on test forms, and |L(φ)| ≤ M_W(X) sup|φ| whenever spt φ ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U. Moreover, for every open W′ ⊆ U,
   sup{L(φ) : φ ∈ K_c(U;ℝ^N), spt φ ⊆ W′, |φ| ≤ 1} = M_{W′}(X):
   "≥" since admissible test forms are such φ; "≤" since for spt φ compact ⊆ W′ the mollifications are admissible for M_{W′} when ε is small, and L(φ) = lim X(ω_ε).
8. (Riesz.) L is a locally bounded linear functional on K_c(U;ℝ^N). By the Riesz Representation Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14`, on the locally compact Hausdorff space U with the finite-dimensional Hilbert space ℝ^N) there are a Radon measure μ_0 on U and a μ_0-measurable ν : U → ℝ^N with |ν| = 1 μ_0-a.e. and L(φ) = ∫ ⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ_0; moreover μ_0 is the total variation measure of L: by (∗) in the proof of 4.14 (the envelope identity sup{L(φ) : |φ| ≤ g} = ∫ g dμ_0 for g ∈ C_c(U), g ≥ 0; SimonGMT `vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure`) and inner regularity of μ_0 on open sets, μ_0(W′) = sup{L(φ) : spt φ ⊆ W′, |φ| ≤ 1} for every open W′ ⊆ U. By step 7, μ_0(W′) = M_{W′}(X) for every open W′ ⊆ U. Define the Borel measure μ on ℝ^P by μ(B) := μ_0(B ∩ U), and replace ν by a Borel function equal to it μ_0-a.e. Then μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 and μ(W) = M_W(X) for every W ⊂⊂ U, i.e. IsMassMeasure X μ.
9. (Representation.) Let v(x) be the k-vector with coefficients v^I(x) := ν_I(x) for x ∈ U (v := 0 off U), i.e. v(x)(α) := Σ_I α(e_I) ν_I(x). For ω ∈ D^k(U): |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| |ν(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖ 1_{tsupport ω}(x) μ-a.e., which is μ-integrable since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and μ is finite on it; and X(ω) = L(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ. So (μ, v) is a measure representation of X, with |v|_* = 1 μ-a.e.
10. (Existence of restrictions.) For a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P put S_A(ω) := ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ. S_A is linear on D^k(U); it is sequentially continuous: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for a fixed compact K ⊆ U and ω_j → 0 uniformly), then |S_A(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖ μ(K) → 0. Thus S_A ∈ D_k(U) and IsRestriction X A S_A holds via the representation (μ, v).
11. (Mass identity.) Let S be any restriction of X to a set A (so A is measurable) and W ⊆ U open. By (R1), S = S_A.
   "≤": for admissible ω (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), S_A(ω) ≤ ∫_{A∩W} |ω||v|_* dμ ≤ μ(W ∩ A).
   "≥": let K ⊆ A ∩ W be compact and ε > 0. By Lusin's theorem (μ_0 Radon, ν measurable) there is a compact K′ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K′) < ε such that ν|_{K′} is continuous and |ν| = 1 on K′; by outer regularity there is an open O with K′ ⊆ O, closure(O) compact ⊆ W, μ(O ∖ K′) < ε. Extend ν|_{K′} (Tietze, componentwise), compose with the radial retraction of ℝ^N onto its closed unit ball and multiply by a cutoff in C_c(O) equal to 1 on K′: this gives φ ∈ K_c(U;ℝ^N) with spt φ ⊆ O, |φ| ≤ 1, φ = ν on K′. Then ∫_A ⟨φ,ν⟩ dμ ≥ μ(K′) − μ(O ∖ K′) ≥ μ(K) − 2ε. The mollifications ω_ε of φ are admissible for M_W for small ε and converge to φ uniformly with supports in closure(O), so S_A(ω_ε) → ∫_A ⟨φ,ν⟩ dμ (dominated convergence). Hence M_W(S) ≥ μ(K) − 2ε. By inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_0 on the Borel set A ∩ W ⊆ U (valid also when μ(A ∩ W) = ∞, U being σ-compact), the supremum of μ(K) over compact K ⊆ A ∩ W is μ(W ∩ A). So M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A).
12. Steps 8, 10, 11 give (R2). Together with (R0) and (R1) this proves the three conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: (R0): testing with φ dx^I (φ = 1 near closure W) bounds M_W(X) by Σ_I ∫_{closure W}|v^I| dμ.
(R1): the coefficient signed measures of two representations agree on C_c^∞(U), hence on C_c(U), hence as measures (Riesz uniqueness), so the restrictions agree.
(R2): by the mass bound X extends to continuous compactly supported forms; the Riesz Representation Theorem (Ch. 1, 4.14) gives μ and ν with |ν| = 1 and μ(W′) = M_{W′}(X).
S_A(ω) := ∫_A⟨ω,v⟩dμ is a current and a restriction of X to A.
Mass identity M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A): '≤' from |v|_* = 1, '≥' by Lusin approximation, mollification and inner regularity.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0,∞). η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x). 1. (Change of variables under the blow-up.) Fix r > 0. The map η_{x,r} is an affine bijection of ℝ^P (a translation followed by the dilation by r⁻¹) with inverse z ↦ x + r z, and for every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n} Hⁿ(A): Hausdorff measure is translation invariant and scales by λⁿ under the dilation y ↦ λy (Mathlib `hausdorffMeasure_smul`, `hausdorffMeasure_smul_right_image`; the constant c_n does not matter). Equivalently, the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞A under the measurable equivalence η_{x,r} is rⁿ·Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(A). Hence, for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ,
   ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_A g(η_{x,r}(z)) dHⁿ(z),
   both sides being integrable or not simultaneously (change of variables under a measurable equivalence that multiplies the measure by a constant; with the Bochner convention both sides are 0 in the non-integrable case).
2. Applying step 1 with A = M and g(y) := f(y) θ(x + r y), and using x + r·η_{x,r}(z) = z, we get for every r > 0
   I_{M,θ}(r) = r^{−n} ∫_M f(η_{x,r}(z)) θ(z) dHⁿ(z) = r^{−n} ∫ f(η_{x,r}(z)) (1_M θ)(z) dHⁿ(z),
   and the same formula for (M′, θ′). The second equality (integral over M = integral of the indicator) uses that M is Hⁿ-null-measurable (Mathlib `integral_indicator₀`); this hypothesis is essential: for a non-measurable M (e.g. a Bernstein set) the restricted measure Hⁿ⌞M and the lower integral of 1_M can disagree, and the statement would fail.

   |I_{M,θ}(r) − I_{M′,θ′}(r)| = r^{−n} |∫ f(η_{x,r}(z)) (1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′)(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| dHⁿ,
   because |f∘η_{x,r}| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ · 1_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}. By hypothesis (applied with this R) the right side tends to 0 as r ↓ 0 (in ℝ≥0∞, hence eventually finite and then tending to 0 as real numbers). So I_{M,θ}(r) − I_{M′,θ′}(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
5. Since θ(x) = θ′(x), the two prescribed limits θ(x)∫_Q f dHⁿ and θ′(x)∫_Q f dHⁿ coincide. By step 4, I_{M,θ}(r) tends to this number if and only if I_{M′,θ′}(r) does. As f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ) was arbitrary, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q holds if and only if HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ x Q holds, for every subspace Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Change of variables under the blow-up η_{x,r}: ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A g∘η_{x,r} dHⁿ (translation invariance and scaling of Hausdorff measure).
Using null-measurability of M, M′, the blow-up integrals equal r^{−n}∫ f((z−x)/r)(1_Mθ)(z) dHⁿ(z) and are integrable for r < ρ/R (spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0)).
Their difference is at most ‖f‖_∞ r^{−n}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}|1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| dHⁿ, which tends to 0.
θ(x) = θ′(x) makes the prescribed limits equal, and the dimension conditions coincide, so the two tangent-space conditions are equivalent.

subproblems.title: The mass measure of a current on ℝ^N vanishes off its support and is finite when the mass is finite (Simon 2.8, 2.12)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let X ∈ D_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k) and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N with IsMassMeasure X μ, i.e. μ(ℝ^N ∖ ℝ^N) = 0 and μ(W) = M_W(X) (X.massOn W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^N whose closure is compact (CompactlyContainedOpen W univ). Then (i) μ(ℝ^N ∖ spt X) = 0, where spt X = X.support = ℝ^N ∖ Z(X) and the zero region Z(X) = X.zeroRegion is the union of all open W with compact closure on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 for every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W); and (ii) if M(X) = X.mass < ∞, then μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure μ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k) (μ : Measure (Eucl N)), IsMassMeasure X μ → μ X.supportᶜ = 0 ∧ (X.mass < ∞ → IsFiniteMeasure μ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 5 and 6 of the selected parent's supplied proof (Simon, Ch. 6, 2.8 and 2.12: μ_T(W) = M_W(T) for W ⊂⊂ U and spt T = spt μ_T), specialized to an arbitrary measure μ with IsMassMeasure X μ on U = ℝ^N. Only the inequality μ(ℝ^N) ≤ M(X) is needed for finiteness.

Conventions. ℝ^N := Eucl N; D_k(ℝ^N) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; a test form is an element of TestFormOn univ k (a C^∞ k-form with compact support). M_W(X) := X.massOn W is the supremum, in [0, ∞], of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) over the admissible forms ω (tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x; massAdmissibleOn univ k W); M(X) := X.mass = M_{ℝ^N}(X) by definition. X vanishes on W (X.VanishesOn W) means X(ω) = 0 for every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(X) := X.zeroRegion = ⋃₀ 𝒮 with 𝒮 := {W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ ℝ^N, X vanishes on W}, and spt X := X.support = ℝ^N ∖ Z(X). B_n := ball(0, n) is the open ball.

Fix N, k, X and μ with IsMassMeasure X μ. Its second component says:
 (H) μ(W) = M_W(X) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^N with compact closure (closure W ⊆ ℝ^N holds automatically).

1. (Vanishing open sets have zero mass.) Let W be a set on which X vanishes. Every admissible ω for M_W(X) has tsupport ω ⊆ W, so X(ω) = 0 and ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) = 0. Thus every element of the set whose supremum is M_W(X) equals 0, and M_W(X) = 0 (also when that set is empty).

2. (Complement of the support.) Since spt X = ℝ^N ∖ Z(X), its complement is (spt X)ᶜ = Z(X) = ⋃₀ 𝒮.

3. (Countable subfamily.) Every member of 𝒮 is open and ℝ^N is second countable. By the Lindelöf property for unions of open sets (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable) there is a countable family 𝒯 ⊆ 𝒮 with ⋃₀ 𝒯 = ⋃₀ 𝒮 = Z(X).

4. (Each member is μ-null.) Let W ∈ 𝒯. Then W ∈ 𝒮, so W is open with compact closure, i.e. CompactlyContainedOpen W univ, and X vanishes on W. By (H) and step 1, μ(W) = M_W(X) = 0.

5. (Conclusion (i).) A countable union of μ-null sets is μ-null (measure_sUnion_null_iff). By steps 2–4, μ((spt X)ᶜ) = μ(⋃₀ 𝒯) = 0.

6. (Balls.) Now assume M(X) < ∞. For n ∈ ℕ the ball B_n is open, and closure B_n ⊆ closedBall(0, n), which is compact because ℝ^N is a proper space; hence closure B_n is compact (a closed subset of a compact set) and CompactlyContainedOpen B_n univ holds. By (H), μ(B_n) = M_{B_n}(X).

7. (Monotonicity of mass.) Every form admissible for M_{B_n}(X) is admissible for M_{ℝ^N}(X), so M_{B_n}(X) ≤ M_{ℝ^N}(X) = M(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono). Hence μ(B_n) ≤ M(X) for every n.

8. (Conclusion (ii).) The balls increase with n (ball_subset_ball) and ⋃_n B_n = ℝ^N (iUnion_ball_nat). By continuity of measure from below (Monotone.measure_iUnion), μ(ℝ^N) = sup_n μ(B_n) ≤ M(X) < ∞. Therefore μ is a finite measure, IsFiniteMeasure μ.

Steps 5 and 8 prove the two conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_W(X) = 0 whenever X vanishes on W, since every admissible form then has X(ω) = 0.
(spt X)ᶜ is the zero region ⋃₀ 𝒮 of relatively compact open sets on which X vanishes; by Lindelöf it is a countable union of members of 𝒮.
Each member W has μ(W) = M_W(X) = 0 by IsMassMeasure, so μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0.
Balls B_n are relatively compact, so μ(B_n) = M_{B_n}(X) ≤ M(X).
Continuity from below on B_n ↑ ℝ^N gives μ(ℝ^N) ≤ M(X) < ∞, so μ is finite.

subproblems.title: Uniqueness of the vector measure of a current on ℝ^N on Borel sets (Simon 2.7–2.9)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and X ∈ D_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k). Let (μ₁, v₁) and (μ₂, v₂) be measure representations of X (IsMeasureRepresentation X μ_i v_i: for every test form ω on ℝ^N the function x ↦ v_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-integrable and X(ω) = ∫ v_i(x)(ω(x)) dμ_i). Then (a) ∫_A v₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^N and every test form ω; and (b) ∫_A v₁(x)(α) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₂(x)(α) dμ₂ for every bounded Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^N and every k-covector α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k) (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Eucl N)) (v₁ v₂ : Eucl N → NVector (Eucl N) k), IsMeasureRepresentation X μ₁ v₁ → IsMeasureRepresentation X μ₂ v₂ → (∀ A : Set (Eucl N), MeasurableSet A → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, ∫ x in A, v₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in A, v₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) x) ∂μ₂) ∧ (∀ A : Set (Eucl N), MeasurableSet A → Bornology.IsBounded A → ∀ α : Covector (Eucl N) k, ∫ x in A, v₁ x α ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in A, v₂ x α ∂μ₂)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7 and the uniqueness part of Step 8 of the selected parent's supplied proof (Simon, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9: the vector measure T⃗μ_T is determined by T). The measure-theoretic core of Step 7(b) and Step 8, namely that the set integrals ∫_A v_i(ω) dμ_i of two representations agree, is the sibling local_uniqueness (accepted theorem slicing_representation_unique). Step 7(a)'s test forms φα give the covector version.

Conventions. ℝ^N := Eucl N. A test form is an element of TestFormOn univ k: a k-form ω : ℝ^N → Covector(ℝ^N, k) that is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞, the order ∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) used by IsSmoothForm), has compact support, and has tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^N (automatic). Integrals ∫_A f dμ are Bochner set integrals.

Sibling used. local_uniqueness (slicing_representation_unique): for P, k ∈ ℕ, an open U ⊆ ℝ^P, Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ and maps v₁, v₂ such that x ↦ v_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-integrable for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U k, and an open W with ∫ v₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫ v₂(ω) dμ₂ for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U k with tsupport ω ⊆ W, one has ∫_A v₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₂(ω) dμ₂ for every Borel A and every ω ∈ TestFormOn U k with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

Fix N, k, X and representations (μ₁, v₁), (μ₂, v₂) of X.

1. (Part (a).) Apply local_uniqueness with P := N, U := ℝ^N (open), the given μ₁, μ₂, v₁, v₂ and W := ℝ^N (open).
 - Integrability hypotheses: for every test form ω, x ↦ v_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-integrable. This is the first component of IsMeasureRepresentation X μ_i v_i.
 - Agreement hypothesis: for every test form ω (trivially tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^N), the second components of the two representations give ∫ v₁(ω) dμ₁ = X(ω) = ∫ v₂(ω) dμ₂.
 - Conclusion: for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N and every test form ω (tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^N), ∫_A v₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂. This is (a).

2. (Part (b): a bounding ball.) Let A be a bounded Borel set and α a k-covector. Since A is bounded, A ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some real R (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall).

3. (A smooth cutoff.) The ball B := ball(0, R + 1) is open, the closed ball C := closedBall(0, R) is closed, and C ⊆ B. By the smooth Urysohn lemma on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^N (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, with smoothness order (⊤ : ℕ∞)), there is a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^N → [0, 1] with support φ = B and φ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ C. Every x with φ(x) ≠ 0 lies in B ⊆ closedBall(0, R + 1); hence φ vanishes outside the compact set closedBall(0, R + 1) and φ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).

4. (The test form φα.) Define ω(x) := φ(x)·α. It is C^∞, as the product of the C^∞ function φ with the constant covector α (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const). It has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^N. Hence ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k.

5. (Agreement on A.) For x ∈ A ⊆ C, φ(x) = 1, so ω(x) = α and v_i(x)(ω(x)) = v_i(x)(α) for i = 1, 2. As A is measurable, functions that agree on A have equal set integrals over A (setIntegral_congr_fun), whether or not they are integrable:
 ∫_A v_i(x)(α) dμ_i = ∫_A v_i(x)(ω(x)) dμ_i (i = 1, 2).

6. (Conclusion (b).) By (a) for A and ω, ∫_A v₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₂(ω) dμ₂. Together with step 5:
 ∫_A v₁(x)(α) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_A v₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ = ∫_A v₂(x)(α) dμ₂.
 This is (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a): local_uniqueness with U = W = ℝ^N; its hypotheses are the integrability parts of the two representations and ∫v₁(ω)dμ₁ = X(ω) = ∫v₂(ω)dμ₂.
(b): A ⊆ closedBall(0,R); a C^∞ cutoff φ with support ball(0,R+1) and φ = 1 on closedBall(0,R) has compact support.
ω := φα is a test form, and ω = α on A, so ∫_A v_i(α)dμ_i = ∫_A v_i(ω)dμ_i (setIntegral_congr_fun).
Apply (a) to A and ω.

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces survive restriction to a Borel set almost everywhere (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; Ch. 3, 1.7)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^N. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be Hᵏ-null-measurable and θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M and θ Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N. Let A ⊆ ℝ^N be a Borel set. Then for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-almost every x, every linear subspace L of ℝ^N which is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) is also a weighted approximate tangent space of (M ∩ A, θ) at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl N)) (θ : Eucl N → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) → ∀ A : Set (Eucl N), MeasurableSet A → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)).restrict (M ∩ A)), ∀ L : Submodule ℝ (Eucl N), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (M ∩ A) θ x L
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the orientation argument of Step 9(b) of the selected parent's supplied proof. That argument has two parts. First, the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2)) shows that ν := θHᵏ⌞(M ∖ A) has zero k-dimensional density at Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ A. Second, the blow-up change of variables shows that the blow-up integrals of (M, θ) and (M ∩ A, θ) at such x have the same limit. Here the first part is the sibling zero_density (accepted theorem lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set) and the second is the sibling tangent_locality (accepted theorem iwl_weighted_tangent_locality).

Conventions. ℝ^N := Eucl N, Hᵏ := μHE[k], B̄_s(x) := closedBall x s. ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued lower Lebesgue integral and ‖·‖ₑ the extended norm (‖t‖ₑ = ofReal|t| for real t). 1_E f := E.indicator f. Limits "r → 0+" are along 𝓝[>] 0.

Siblings used.
 - zero_density (lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set). Let W ⊆ ℝ^Q be open, S Hⁿ-null-measurable and g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞] with ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. y with y ∈ W and y ∉ S, (∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} g dHⁿ)/ofReal(ρⁿ) → 0 as ρ → 0+.
 - tangent_locality (iwl_weighted_tangent_locality). Let M, M′ be Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ, θ′ real functions and x a point with θ(x) = θ′(x). Assume that for some ρ > 0, θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and θ′ on M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x). Assume also that for every R > 0, ofReal((rⁿ)⁻¹)·∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′‖ₑ dHⁿ → 0 as r → 0+. Then for every subspace Q, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ x Q.

Fix N, k, M, θ and A as in the statement, and put S := M ∖ A and g(z) := ofReal(θ(z)) ∈ [0, ∞).

1. (Measurability.) A is Borel, so M ∩ A and S = M ∖ A are Hᵏ-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.inter, NullMeasurableSet.diff).

2. (Local finiteness.) Let K be compact. θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K and S ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ K, so θ is integrable on S ∩ K. Since ofReal(θ(z)) ≤ ‖θ(z)‖ₑ, we get ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dHᵏ ≤ ∫⁻_{S∩K} ‖θ‖ₑ dHᵏ < ∞ (lintegral_ofReal_le_lintegral_enorm and finiteness of the integral of an integrable function).

3. (Zero density.) Apply zero_density with Q := N, n := k, W := ℝ^N (open), S and g; the hypothesis is step 2. Writing F_y(ρ) := ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} g dHᵏ, we get: for Hᵏ-a.e. y, if y ∉ S then F_y(ρ)/ofReal(ρᵏ) → 0 as ρ → 0+.

4. (Passing to Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A).) An Hᵏ-a.e. property holds Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae). Since M ∩ A is null-measurable, Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ A (ae_restrict_mem₀). Hence for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x we have both x ∈ M ∩ A and the conclusion of step 3. Fix such an x. As x ∈ A, x ∉ S, and therefore
 (Z) F_x(ρ)/ofReal(ρᵏ) → 0 as ρ → 0+.

5. (The integrand.) For every z, 1_Mθ(z) − 1_{M∩A}θ(z) = 1_Sθ(z): both sides are 0 if z ∉ M or z ∈ M ∩ A, and both equal θ(z) if z ∈ M ∖ A. Since θ > 0 on M ⊇ S, ‖1_Sθ(z)‖ₑ = 1_S g(z). Since S is null-measurable also for Hᵏ⌞B̄_s(x) (a measure below Hᵏ), lintegral_indicator₀ and Measure.restrict_restrict₀ give, for every s,
 ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_{M∩A}θ‖ₑ dHᵏ = ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} 1_S g dHᵏ = F_x(s).

6. (Rescaling.) Let R > 0 and r > 0. Then Rr > 0 and ofReal((Rr)ᵏ) = ofReal(Rᵏ)·ofReal(rᵏ), where 0 < ofReal(Rᵏ) < ∞ and 0 < ofReal(rᵏ) < ∞; also ofReal((rᵏ)⁻¹) = ofReal(rᵏ)⁻¹. Hence
 ofReal((rᵏ)⁻¹)·F_x(Rr) = ofReal(Rᵏ)·[F_x(Rr)/ofReal((Rr)ᵏ)].
 As r → 0+, Rr → 0+ (Rr is continuous in r, vanishes at 0, and is positive for r > 0). By (Z) the bracket tends to 0, and multiplying by the finite constant ofReal(Rᵏ) gives a limit of ofReal(Rᵏ)·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). With step 5:
 ofReal((rᵏ)⁻¹)·∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_{M∩A}θ‖ₑ dHᵏ → 0 as r → 0+, for every R > 0.

7. (Local integrability.) The closed ball B̄_1(x) is compact, so θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_1(x), and hence on its subset (M ∩ A) ∩ B̄_1(x).

8. (Tangent locality.) Apply tangent_locality with P := N, n := k, M, M′ := M ∩ A, θ′ := θ, the point x and ρ := 1. Its hypotheses are: null-measurability (step 1); θ(x) = θ(x); integrability (step 7); and the decay condition (step 6). It yields, for every subspace L, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (M ∩ A) θ x L. The forward implication is the claim at x.

9. (Conclusion.) Steps 4–8 apply at Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x. The exceptional null set does not depend on L, so for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x every weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x is one of (M ∩ A, θ) at x. ∎
proof_key_steps: S := M ∖ A and M ∩ A are Hᵏ-null-measurable; g := ofReal∘θ has ∫⁻_{S∩K} g < ∞ for compact K.
zero_density gives F_x(ρ)/ofReal(ρᵏ) → 0 for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∉ S, hence for Hᵏ⌞(M∩A)-a.e. x (which lies in M ∩ A).
‖1_Mθ − 1_{M∩A}θ‖ₑ = 1_S·ofReal θ (θ > 0 on M), so the blow-up defect integral over B̄_{Rr}(x) equals F_x(Rr).
ofReal((rᵏ)⁻¹)F_x(Rr) = ofReal(Rᵏ)·F_x(Rr)/ofReal((Rr)ᵏ) → 0 as r → 0+.
tangent_locality with M′ = M ∩ A, θ′ = θ, ρ = 1 transfers every weighted tangent space of (M, θ) at x to (M ∩ A, θ).

subproblems.title: Restriction of a rectifiable triple to a Borel set (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1; integer multiplicity of T⌞A)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 in U = ℝ^N: M is μHE[k]-null-measurable and countably k-rectifiable, θ > 0 on M and locally μHE[k]-integrable on M, ξ is μHE[k]⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, and for μHE[k]⌞M-a.e. x, ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_k for an orthonormal τ spanning a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x). Let A ⊆ ℝ^N be a Borel set. Then IsRectifiableTriple univ k (M ∩ A) θ ξ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl N)) (θ : Eucl N → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl N → NVector (Eucl N) k) (A : Set (Eucl N)), IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k M θ ξ → MeasurableSet A → IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k (M ∩ A) θ ξ
proof_key_steps: Subset, null-measurability (M null-measurable, A Borel), countable rectifiability (CountablyRectifiable.mono), positivity and local integrability pass to M ∩ A ⊆ M.
Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A) ≤ Hᵏ⌞M transfers a.e. strong measurability of ξ and the a.e. orientation data of (M, θ, ξ).
tangent_inter turns HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) into the same for (M ∩ A, θ) at Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x, with the same τ and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ.
